name: Chemical Splash
overview: Fertilizers, cleaning agents, fuels, and other farm chemicals can splash on skin or into eyes. Flush immediately.

steps.title: Move from source
steps.detail: Get the person away from the chemical to prevent further exposure.

steps.title: Flush skin
steps.detail: Remove contaminated clothing. Rinse skin with water for at least 15–20 minutes.

steps.title: Flush eyes
steps.detail: Hold eyelids open and rinse with clean water for 15–20 minutes. Use an eye wash station if available.

steps.title: Check the label
steps.detail: Some chemicals have specific first aid instructions. Follow them if you have the container.

when_to_seek_help: Call 911 if: severe pain, vision changes, large skin area affected, or chemical was swallowed. Call poison control (1-800-222-1222) for guidance on milder exposures.
prevention_tips: Wear goggles and chemical-resistant gloves when handling chemicals.
Have an eyewash station and emergency shower near chemical storage.
Store chemicals in labeled containers away from food and water.
